**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use default pg import in the migration CLI**

When `pnpm --filter @aiops/devops db:migrate` executes this ESM file, `pg` is a CommonJS package and does not expose a runtime named `Pool` export; the added local declaration only makes TypeScript accept it. The CLI will abort at module load before reading `DATABASE_URL`, so no migrations can run. Use the same default import pattern as the server package, e.g. `import pg from "pg"; const { Pool } = pg;`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin migrations to one pg client**

The CLI calls `applyMigrations(pool, ...)`, so this transaction is issued through `Pool.query`; that API does not reserve one connection across the `BEGIN`, migration SQL, version insert, and `COMMIT`. If a later statement is run on a different client or fails after DDL has executed, the database can be left with partially applied schema changes but no matching `schema_migrations` row, contrary to the runbook's transactional guarantee. Check out a single `PoolClient` with `pool.connect()` for the migration loop and release it afterward.
